why: proof_coverage now reads a crossing's proven_by as one-or-many, because a seam has ends in more than one component — but clearance.clear calls standing(proven_by) on a single path, and transitions.py's the_named_proof_stands_in_proven_space lane does the same, so a list is a TypeError at the door. The gate therefore checks ONE of the proofs a crossing record names, and the sieve that judges coverage checks all of them: the record can claim more than the gate verified

occurrences.found: 2026-09-07, crossing 9579a6f9cec6 BUILDME->PROVEME, the first crossing to name three proofs
occurrences.second_field_that_would_move: proven_seal_date is singular; with many proofs it is either a list or the newest, and the_witness_agrees_with_the_seal_it_names compares it to one seal
occurrences.why_not_fixed_in_place: the gate is a machine with its own proofs and its own ticket; slipping a signature change into an unrelated crossing is the shape Law 8 refuses
occurrences.workaround_used: cleared onto the seam's OWNING component (trouble's own proof); the other two named in the ticket's crossings[].proven_by and in the journal under also_proven_by; all three verified current by pc.lacks (0 lacks)
